title: Black Light FTL Route Safety Integration Registry
purpose: Bridge EXO FTL route environments to versioned safety calibration and certification. Physically resolved route paths take precedence when supplied and are certified interval-by-interval through the selected family; uncertainty-aware conservative blocker envelopes are preserved only when a provenance-bearing topology-hazard applicability authority links the physical precursor to the certified family hazard. Identity context, installation readiness, maintenance state, and common-cause power/thermal/support transients are forwarded into installation timing authority before certification. Single-point SI gravity/curvature inputs are secondary, while PROPOSED normalized route archetypes remain fallback-only when no physical packet exists.

designIntentSource.title: The different lightspeed methods
designIntentSource.scope: Family-specific gravity/miscalculation behavior, safety lookahead, emergency de-transit, increasing maturity margins, non-perfect safety, and mathematically credible environmental and machinery underlays.

authority.statusRule: Supplied physical route paths outrank single-point physical environments; supplied single-point physical environments outrank route archetypes. Invalid or unresolved supplied physical evidence blocks fallback. Route archetype packets are PROPOSED simulation mappings used only when no physical route/path environment is supplied. Installation condition modifies timing/readiness/recovery authority downstream of environmental physics and may not alter family identity or external gravity.

deep-space.notes: Fallback comparison environment only; not a physical deep-space measurement.

planetary-well.notes: Fallback normalized planetary-well model, not a universal planetary constant.

gas-giant.notes: Fallback route model; magnetic/plasma observability remains separate from gravity.

binary.notes: Fallback binary model emphasizing time-varying competing gradients over raw potential.

compact-object.notes: Fallback-only. If real compact-object inputs violate weak-field validity, OUTSIDE_MODEL_VALIDITY blocks certification rather than using this finite archetype.

q-disturbed.notes: Fallback higher-dimensional boundary/model uncertainty archetype; exotic boundary terms remain fictional/derived.

topologyHazardApplicability.rule: Applicability must resolve from canon/provenance. The route-safety adapter forwards identity fields unchanged to family-segment certification; it does not infer them from presentation labels and does not substitute a boolean. No match is UNRESOLVED, contradiction is CONFLICT, SUPPORTING_PHYSICAL_PRECURSOR is non-blocking, and raw caller booleans are not authority.

installationConditionAuthority.rule: Installation condition is resolved before family/segment certification. Shared power, thermal, cooling, hydraulic, dielectric or metabolic evidence may reduce multiple readiness channels together. Blocking or conflicting condition authority stops certification; condition evidence never selects an FTL family or changes external gravity.

integrationRules: The adapter must preserve the generated family and must never use certification to auto-select a different family.
When physicalRoutePathContext, pathPacket, or segmentPacket is supplied, route safety must use family-segment certification and must not collapse the route back into a single-point certificate.

Route safety must forward namedTechnologyId, vesselId, installationId, raceId, manufacturerId, canonicalResolutionRequired, topologyHazardKey, any pre-resolved applicability packet, and any explicitly simulation-only applicability override into family-segment certification without replacing those fields with a caller boolean.
Route safety must forward measured installation readiness, maintenance state and common-cause transient/coupling evidence into installation timing authority before certification.

Identity fields are provenance selectors, not family selectors: race/species, vessel, manufacturer or installation identity may select a more specific applicability record only after the transit family/hazard is independently established.
Common-cause readiness aggregation is deterministic machinery modeling rather than a failure-probability calculation; correlated deficits may not be multiplied as though independent.

A declared hard power-buffer or thermal operating limit may block safety-critical channels when supported by supplied telemetry and limit/horizon data; missing telemetry must remain missing rather than guessed.
Family-certified route disposition is conjunctive across required intervals; later benign intervals cannot erase an earlier blocker.

The first blocking interval, nominal distance/time to blocker, authorized conservative distance/time to blocker, intervention reachability, topology-hazard applicability provenance, and installation timing provenance must survive into the route-level result.

A normalized-degeneracy or topology boundary may move the conservative planning edge earlier only when the topology-hazard applicability authority resolves a matching REQUIRED_PHYSICAL_PRECURSOR relationship to the already-certified hazard. Otherwise it remains displayable evidence but cannot alter route certification.
A SUPPORTING_PHYSICAL_PRECURSOR may influence sensing, maintenance, diagnostics and confidence but does not generically move a certified blocker earlier.
For PRECOMMIT families, a topology boundary may constrain endpoint/location evidence but may not create an intermediate local FTL velocity; prediction-time authority remains governing.

For exotic families, missing family-boundary hazard remains unresolved unless explicitly established as known absent; route archetype boundary values may not be injected into a physical route path as though measured.

When physicalEnvironmentContext is supplied without a physical route path, gravity/curvature terms must be resolved by the physical environment bridge and must not be replaced by route archetype numbers.
A supplied physical packet that is PARTIAL, UNRESOLVED, or OUTSIDE_MODEL_VALIDITY is a blocking result; fallback is prohibited.
Only absence of physical route-path and physicalEnvironmentContext inputs permits use of PROPOSED normalized route archetypes.
Route archetype values are PROPOSED normalized simulation inputs, not measured astrophysical constants.
Physical SI values with unlike dimensions must be normalized by an explicit versioned profile before entering the dimensionless family-severity function.
Family-boundary hazard remains fictional/operator-specific and is additive to the real-physics environment rather than derived from ordinary gravity alone.
Calibration profile identity/version and physical-normalization profile identity/version must be copied into any certificate that depends on them.
REJECTED, UNRESOLVED, OUTSIDE_MODEL_VALIDITY, and CONFLICT states must survive into presentation and export.
A generated speed/range value is capability modeling, not proof that the selected route is certified safe.
Family-specific required hazards are additive to route hazards.
Higher maturity may improve lookahead, covariance, redundancy, and recovery margins but cannot suppress a governing hard hazard.
Named-source unresolved overrides remain unresolved and may not inherit the generic family baseline as named canon.
canonGuards: Do not describe PROPOSED route archetype numbers as real astrophysical measurements.
Do not describe versioned normalization references or generic coupling coefficients as constants of nature.
Do not convert route difficulty into a universal FTL constant.
Do not collapse a physically sampled route into one representative point when interval evidence is available.
Do not invent a family-boundary hazard from ordinary gravity or from a generic route archetype for a physical path.
Do not promote a physical topology boundary into an FTL blocker without a provenance-bearing REQUIRED_PHYSICAL_PRECURSOR authority connecting it to the certified hazard.
Do not substitute a raw boolean for canonical topology-hazard applicability.

Do not infer family identity from named technology terminology, race/species identity, machinery ancestry, manufacturer, vessel class or installation identity unless an authority explicitly establishes that mapping.
Do not infer independent failure probabilities from readiness or common-cause coupling values.
Do not use machinery thermal/power stress as evidence that a fictional FTL hazard exists.
Do not certify a route when calibration or supplied physical validity is unresolved or conflicting.
Do not hide REJECTED, UNRESOLVED, or OUTSIDE_MODEL_VALIDITY behind a generated performance number.
Do not infer a named civilization or installation limit from the generic simulation baseline.
Do not turn a selected UI family into evidence for an unresolved archaeological family.
Do not claim perfect safety at any path maturity.
Do not spend protected recovery reserve to improve nominal advertised performance.
